evidence: The Roland Space Echo is named consistently in accounts of the Black Ark's signal chain, alongside the Mutron phaser, and Perry's use of runaway tape feedback as a live gesture rather than a fixed setting is described in numerous interviews and studio histories. Held at consensus because no first-hand source is named here (Q22).

earlier.title: RE-201 Space Echo, as sold to guitarists

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Pick one snare hit and follow it. It repeats, and each repeat is slightly duller and slightly less in tune than the one before, because it is a tape loop wearing the sound down every pass. Then listen for the places where the repeats stop dying away and start feeding on themselves, piling up into a howl before somebody pulls them back. That is a hand on a knob, decided in the moment.

explanation.age7: An echo box that repeats sounds, pushed so far that the repeats take over the whole record.
explanation.age13: Inside the Space Echo is a loop of tape and three heads reading it, so a sound comes back several times, each copy a bit more worn than the last. Turn the feedback up far enough and the repeats feed themselves and build into a roar instead of fading. Perry used that as something you do at a particular moment, like hitting a drum, rather than a setting chosen before you start.
explanation.adult: The RE-201 earns a node because its failure mode is musical and its controls are performable. Self-oscillation at high feedback, plus the pitch instability of a tape loop under load, give dub its smearing and its runaway bloom. Roland engineered for stability and reliability and shipped an instrument without meaning to.

demoCaption.age13: Switch the echo in, then turn the repeats up. Each echo comes back a little duller than the one before, the way a tape echo wears the sound down. Push the repeats far enough and they stop fading and start building on each other. Perry used that as something to do at a particular moment, like hitting a drum, not a setting left alone.
demoCaption.adult: The echo sits on a send beside the dry drums, with a filter and soft saturation in its feedback loop, roughly what a Space Echo's worn tape does to each repeat. It is not a model of the RE-201's circuit. For Perry the feedback control is the point: ridden by hand, it turns an effect into a part played in the moment.
